summary: Qian Lin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at Fudan University, Bristol, and the University of Washington under teachers including Richard G. Salomon, Collett Cox, and Rupert Gethin, and held a post at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem.

Qiang Ning is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. Supervised by Hung Wu and Irene Winter, Ning studied at UCAS and Warwick, held research posts at the Dunhuang Academy, and taught at San Diego State, Michigan, and Yale.

Qichao Liang (1873–1929) was a scholar in sinology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied under Youwei Kang and at Xuehai Tang. He headed the Translation Bureau and National Library of China, and taught at the Current Affairs Academy, Tsinghua, and Nankai.

Qing Duan (1953–2022) specialized in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Peking University and the University of Hamburg under Ronald Eric Emmerick, Xianlin Ji, and Zhongxin Jiang, she served as a professor at Peking University (~1987–2022).

Qingying Chen (1942–2022) worked in Tibetology and history/archaeology. Educated at Qinghai Nationalities University and Minzu University of China under Wang Yao, he taught physics, worked at Minzu University, and served as director of the Historical Research Institute at the China Tibetology Research Center.

Qingzhi Zhu works in linguistics, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He earned degrees from Northwest Normal University, Central China Normal University, and Sichuan University, and held professorial posts at Peking University (1998–2014) and the Education University of Hong Kong (attested 2010).
Qinni Liu is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin.
Qiwen Xiao is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied for a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yongdong Shi (attested 2013).

Quentin Devers works in history, archaeology, and Tibetology. He served as a research assistant at the University of Virginia (2008–2010), an archaeologist at Heritage WA (2012), and became a chargé de recherche at the CNRS in 2016.
R. Balasubramanian (1929–2017) was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under Varahur Kalyanasundara Sastri and served as Director at the University of Madras (~1976–1989).

R. D. Vadekar (1902–1986) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Shripad Krishna Belvalkar. He served as Professor of Sanskrit and Allied Languages at Fergusson College (attested 1958).
R. Gayathri is an Indology scholar who studied as a Ph.D. scholar at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute under doctoral supervisor V. Yamuna Devi (attested 2026).

R. Gordon Wasson (1898–1986) was an author in religious studies and Indology who studied at the London School of Economics and Columbia University. He worked as a journalist and spent his main career at J.P. Morgan & Co. (1934–1963).

R. H. Blyth (1898–1964) worked in Japanology and Buddhist studies. After studying at the University of London (~1919–1923), he held academic posts at Keijo Imperial University (~1925–1940) and Kanazawa University (~1940–1941).

R. H. Tawney (1880–1962) was a historian who studied at Rugby School and Balliol College, Oxford. He held teaching posts at the University of Glasgow (~1906–1908) and the London School of Economics (~1917–1949).

R. K. Bodhe studied at the R.C. Patel Institute of Pharmaceutical Education and Research (2017–2019) and served as Research Officer at the Kaivalyadhama Health and Yoga Research Center (attested 2005) in the field of Indology.
R. Keller Kimbrough works in Japanology and religious studies. He earned a PhD from Yale University and held a post at the University of Colorado Boulder (attested 2013).
R. N. Gadre was an Indology scholar who held posts as Professor of Sanskrit at Sir Parashurambhau College and Savitribai Phule Pune University (both attested 1958).
R. P. Paranjpye (1876–1966) studied under Vaman Shivram Apte and served as Vice-Chancellor of Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 1959).

R. Ramanujachari was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who served as Professor of Philosophy at Annamalai University (attested 1938–1940) and as editor of the Journal of the Annamalai University (attested 1950).
